original_value: Pneumocccal pneumonia, a secondary bacterial infection that follows influenza A infection, is responsible for morbidity and mortality in children, elderly, and immunocomprised groups. A mathematical model to study the global stability of pneumococcal pneumonia with awareness and saturated treatment is presented. The basic reproduction number, R0, is computed using the next generation matrix method. The results show that if R0<1, the disease-free steady state is locally asymptotically stable; thus, pneumococcal pneumonia would be eradicated in the population. On the other hand, if R0>1 the endemic steady state is globally attractive; thus, the disease would persist in the population. The quadratic-linear and Goh–Voltera Lyapunov functionals approach are used to prove the global stabilities of the disease-free and endemic steady states, respectively. The sensitivity analysis of R0 on model parameters shows that, it is positively sensitive to the maximal effective rate before antibiotic resistance awareness, rate of relapse encountered in administering treatment, and loss of information by aware susceptible individuals. Contrarily, the sensitivity analysis of R0 on model parameters is negatively sensitive to recovery rate due to treatment and the rate at which unaware susceptible individuals become aware. The numerical analysis of the model shows that awareness about antibiotic resistance and treatment plays a significant role in the control of pneumococcal pneumonia.

result.paraphrase: Pneumococcal pneumonia, a secondary bacterial infection that follows influenza A infection, causes morbidity and mortality in children, the elderly, and immunocompromised groups. This paper presents a mathematical model for examining the global stability of pneumococcal pneumonia with awareness and saturated treatment. The basic reproduction number, R0, is calculated by the next generation matrix method. The results indicate that when R0<1, the disease-free steady state is locally asymptotically stable; hence pneumococcal pneumonia will be eliminated from the population. Conversely, when R0>1, the endemic steady state is globally attractive; thus the disease will persist in the population. Quadratic-linear and Goh–Voltera Lyapunov functionals are used to establish the global stability of the disease-free and endemic steady states, respectively. Sensitivity analysis of R0 with respect to model parameters shows positive sensitivity to the maximal effective rate before antibiotic resistance awareness, the relapse rate encountered during treatment, and the loss of information among aware susceptible individuals. In contrast, R0 is negatively sensitive to the recovery rate due to treatment and the rate at which unaware susceptible individuals become aware. Numerical analysis of the model demonstrates that awareness of antibiotic resistance and treatment plays a significant role in controlling pneumococcal pneumonia.
